change: Parse String-owned bytes without cloning the input; release the buffer-table borrow before calling existing result constructors.

contract.before: Validate and clone String storage, trim and parse the copy, then call the current Integer or Float constructor.
contract.after: Validate and borrow String storage, perform the same pure trim and parse, release the borrow, then call the same constructor.
preserved: Only the String owner reads its byte buffers. Id and all object representations are unchanged.
Integer limits, float fallback, UTF-8 validation, four-byte whitespace set, invalid-input nil, and invalid-receiver errors are unchanged.
Dependency access and current Word, Integer and Float constructors remain live. No borrow spans a message or GC callback.

microbenchmark.scope: Existing asInteger and asNumber through Id, input sizes 16 bytes/4 KiB/1 MiB. Leading whitespace followed by integer/float, and invalid UTF-8 at the beginning of the buffer. Serial ABBA, five samples/process. Automatic GC disabled only for timed work; precise GC outside samples. Results checked.

limits: Controlled library substitution into the previous exact benchmark prefix, not a fresh release installation. Only the String library differs across 783 files.

Serial ABBA, two fresh processes per variant and five samples per case per process; thread CPU clock. Result construction is timed; input creation and explicit GC are not. Automatic GC is disabled only for bounded benchmark work. Runtime policy stays unchanged.

Short successful parsing is effectively unchanged (+0.6% Integer, -0.6% Float). Large whitespace-padded parsing uses 2-4% less CPU. Large early-invalid UTF-8 avoids a whole-buffer copy; this is not an application-wide speedup.
No concurrent test/build workloads were launched by this task during measurement; unrelated host processes remained active.
validation: Candidate text_error and numbers integration tests passed, including signed limits, overflow fallback, invalid bytes, whitespace distinctions, receiver validation and replaced constructors that collect.
Expanded text_error also passed against the baseline library, independently checking preservation of existing behavior.

scripts/oop-id-slice-test.sh passed: owner unit tests, compiler/GC smoke, negative direct-dispatch and construction contracts, cross-thread rejection, export audit, independent C cold caller and finalizer containment.
contract_review: The removed host Vec was used only by callback-free Rust parsing. Both successful integer and float paths now explicitly drop the buffer borrow before any result-construction message. All early failures return while Rust releases the borrow. No message was removed, cached or reordered.
